venues.name: Le Bristol Paris
venues.note: The grande dame of them all, a courtyard garden hidden behind the city's most powerful street.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel George V
venues.note: The Four Seasons standard our members already trust, wrapped in legendary flowers.

venues.name: Le Meurice, Dorchester Collection
venues.note: Starck's hand over an 18th-century bones, looking straight onto the gardens.

venues.name: Hôtel Plaza Athénée, Dorchester Collection
venues.note: The couture address, Dior at the door and the red awnings on the avenue.

venues.name: Cheval Blanc Paris
venues.area: 1st arr. / La Samaritaine, by the Seine
venues.note: LVMH's newest icon, river light, a Dior spa, and a pool most hotels can only envy.

venues.name: Hôtel de Crillon, A Rosewood Hotel
venues.note: An 18th-century palace on the grandest square, restored without losing its nerve.

venues.name: Le Royal Monceau – Raffles Paris
venues.area: 8th arr. / near the Arc de Triomphe
venues.note: The artist's palace, Starck design, its own gallery and cinema, a long quiet pool.

venues.name: La Réserve Paris
venues.area: 8th arr. / Avenue Gabriel, by the Élysée
venues.note: A forty-key mansion that feels less like a hotel and more like a private house.

venues.name: Shangri-La Paris
venues.note: A Bonaparte prince's palace, with the Eiffel Tower filling many of the windows.

venues.name: The Peninsula Paris
venues.area: 16th arr. / near the Arc de Triomphe
venues.note: Peninsula precision and a rooftop that trades on the finest view in Paris.

venues.name: Bulgari Hotel Paris
venues.note: Italian glamour dropped onto the smartest corner, with one of the city's largest hotel spas.

venues.name: Hôtel Lutetia
venues.note: The only Palace on the Left Bank, literary Saint-Germain in an Art Deco landmark.

venues.name: Hôtel Fouquet's Paris, Barrière
venues.note: Family-owned Barrière glamour above the most famous brasserie on the avenue.

venues.name: The Ritz Paris
venues.note: The most famous hotel name in the world, still keeping the promise on Place Vendôme.

venues.name: Maison Villeroy
venues.note: A discreet townhouse near the Élysée for members who prefer to be unseen.

venues.name: Saint James Paris, Relais & Châteaux
venues.area: 16th arr. / near the Bois de Boulogne
venues.note: The only château-hotel in Paris, set behind its own gardens.

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental, Paris
venues.note: A garden courtyard hidden off the smartest shopping street, run to the group's quiet precision.

venues.name: Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme
venues.note: Refined and understated, a calm base a step from the jewellers of Vendôme.

venues.name: J.K. Place Paris
venues.note: Italian-run, jewel-box luxury on the Left Bank, warm where the palaces can be grand.

venues.name: Nolinski Paris, Evok Collection
venues.note: A chic forty-five-key house between the Louvre and the Palais Royal.

venues.name: Brach Paris, Evok Collection
venues.note: Starck-designed and buzzing, with a rooftop garden and a fashionable crowd.

venues.name: Grand Powers
venues.note: Elegant, intimate and perfectly placed for a day among the maisons.

venues.name: Le Burgundy Paris
venues.note: Refined and central, with a spa and a Michelin-recognised kitchen of its own.

venues.name: Château Voltaire
venues.note: A fashion-crowd design hotel that hides its glamour behind a plain door.

venues.name: Maison Proust
venues.note: Belle Époque opulence and a La Mer spa, tucked into the Marais.

venues.name: Le Grand Mazarin
venues.note: Joyful maximalism and one of the liveliest hotel restaurants in town.

venues.name: La Fantaisie
venues.note: A garden-inspired newcomer with a rooftop and a light-hearted spirit.

venues.name: Maison Delano Paris
venues.note: Sleek and discreet, arranged around a quiet courtyard.

venues.name: Le Pavillon de la Reine
venues.note: Hidden behind the loveliest square in Paris, romantic and quiet.

venues.name: Monsieur George
venues.note: A warm, well-placed boutique with more soul than its size suggests.

venues.name: Grand Hôtel du Palais Royal
venues.area: 1st arr. / by the Palais Royal gardens
venues.note: Elegant and superbly placed, a step from the arcades of the Palais Royal.

venues.name: Relais Christine
venues.note: A hushed Left Bank townhouse built around its own courtyard.

venues.name: Kei
venues.note: A Japanese hand on French cooking, exact to the millimetre, one of the city's nine three-stars.

venues.name: Plénitude – Cheval Blanc Paris
venues.area: 1st arr. / La Samaritaine, by the Seine
venues.note: Sauces treated as the whole point, in a room that looks out over the river.

venues.name: Arpège
venues.note: The garden on the plate, Passard's near-vegan turn is the finest veg-friendly table at this height.

venues.name: Le Cinq
venues.note: Classical French haute in a palace dining room, the grand occasion, done properly.

venues.name: Épicure – Le Bristol
venues.note: French haute cuisine facing Le Bristol's garden, serene, precise, timeless.

venues.name: Pierre Gagnaire
venues.area: 8th arr. / Rue Balzac, near the Champs-Élysées
venues.note: The avant-garde of modern French cooking, three stars held since 1996.

venues.name: Le Gabriel – La Réserve Paris
venues.note: Intimate three-star cooking inside one of the city's most private houses.

venues.name: Alléno Paris au Pavillon Ledoyen
venues.note: A pavilion in the Champs-Élysées gardens, and Alléno's modern French at full stretch.

venues.name: Le Pré Catelan
venues.note: A belle-époque pavilion set deep in the park, one of the loveliest tables in Paris.

venues.name: Restaurant Guy Savoy – Monnaie de Paris
venues.area: 6th arr. / on the Seine, the former Mint
venues.note: The most-decorated name in the city by La Liste, in a riverside palace.

venues.name: Table by Bruno Verjus
venues.note: The international ticket of the moment, produce-led cooking from the counter.

venues.name: L'Ambroisie
venues.note: Old-guard grandeur on the most beautiful square in Paris.

venues.name: Le Clarence
venues.note: A private mansion, a Bordeaux cellar to match, and cooking of real depth.

venues.name: La Scène
venues.note: Stéphanie Le Quellec's precise modern French, one of the city's top kitchens.

venues.name: David Toutain
venues.note: Vegetable-forward modern French, curious and quietly brilliant.

venues.name: Le Taillevent
venues.note: A grande-maison institution, classical to its bones.

venues.name: Le Grand Restaurant – Jean-François Piège
venues.note: A jewel-box room and Piège's exacting modern French.

venues.name: L'Orangerie – Four Seasons George V
venues.note: The George V's lighter, luminous second table, no less serious for it.

venues.name: L'Abysse au Pavillon Ledoyen
venues.note: A sushi counter of rare finesse, within Alléno's pavilion.

venues.name: L'Oiseau Blanc – The Peninsula Paris
venues.note: French cooking on the rooftop, with the Eiffel Tower for company.

venues.name: Le Jules Verne
venues.note: Dinner inside the Eiffel Tower itself, the view every first visit wants.

venues.name: Maison Rostang
venues.note: Old-school luxury and classical French in Art Nouveau rooms.

venues.name: Alliance
venues.area: 5th arr. / Left Bank, near the Seine
venues.note: Restrained, precise modern French with none of the theatre.

venues.name: Sushi Yoshinaga
venues.note: An omakase counter working with fish of exceptional quality.

venues.name: Septime
venues.note: The most coveted mid-price reservation in Paris, seasonal, confident, warm.

venues.name: Frenchie
venues.note: Greg Marchand's intimate, buzzing bistronomy, small room, big following.

venues.name: Benoit
venues.note: The only Michelin-starred bistro in Paris, Belle Époque, and run by Ducasse.

venues.name: Allard
venues.note: Escargots, sole meunière and a 1900s room, the Paris bistro, preserved.

venues.name: Sharma Ji
venues.note: The one genuinely Michelin-listed Indian in Paris, refined, and never a cliché.

venues.name: Desi Road
venues.area: 6th arr. / Rue Dauphine, near Pont Neuf
venues.note: A glamorous Indian bistro on the Left Bank with real vegetarian breadth.

venues.name: Le Comptoir du Relais
venues.note: The cult bistronomy address, a small counter that shaped a whole movement.

venues.name: Chez L'Ami Jean
venues.note: A lively Basque institution, generous cooking and a legendary riz au lait.

venues.name: Le Baratin
venues.note: The birthplace of bistronomy, still personal, still priced with restraint.

venues.name: Le Bon Georges
venues.note: Produce and wine of unusual seriousness, in a warm neighbourhood room.

venues.name: Pierre Sang in Oberkampf
venues.note: Surprise tasting menus at an open kitchen, French technique, Korean soul.

venues.name: Bistrot Paul Bert
venues.note: The bistro of the imagination, steak-frites, soufflé, a wall of wine.

venues.name: Clamato
venues.note: Septime's seafood sibling, small plates, natural wine, no reservations.

venues.name: Double Dragon
venues.note: The Levha sisters' playful pan-Asian, bright, fun, generous.

venues.name: Le Radis Beurre
venues.note: Warm bistronomy and a blackboard menu, at a price that flatters the cooking.

venues.name: Le Grand Bain
venues.note: Creative small plates and natural wine in an easy, buzzy room.

venues.name: Les Canailles
venues.note: Simple French cooking done exactly right, the food a French grandmother would make.

venues.name: Le Pantruche
venues.note: A 1940s bistro mood and a short, seasonal menu that rarely misses.

venues.name: Au Bon Accueil
venues.note: Seasonal bistro cooking and a terrace that looks straight at the tower.

venues.name: Mensae
venues.note: French comfort cooking with real value, a neighbourhood room worth the trip.

venues.name: Kokoro
venues.note: A Franco-Japanese couple's regional French, touched lightly by Japan.

venues.name: Lao Siam
venues.note: A flavour tour of Laos and Thailand, credentialed and unpretentious.

venues.name: Chez Michel
venues.note: A 1939 institution of Breton-leaning bistronomy, in a Japanese chef's careful hands.

venues.name: Impérial Choisy
venues.note: Cantonese cooking done cleanly and well, in the heart of Paris's Chinatown.

venues.name: Mandoobar
venues.note: A tiny counter given over to Korean dumplings, made with real care.

venues.name: Eiffel Tower
venues.note: The city's iron heart; go to the summit at dusk and catch the on-the-hour sparkle, or dine at the Jules Verne on the second floor for a table above Paris.
credentials: most-visited paid monument in the world

venues.name: Arc de Triomphe
venues.note: Climb the 284 steps to a rooftop where twelve avenues fan out like a star, with the Champs-Élysées running straight to the Louvre.

venues.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
venues.note: Reopened December 2024 after the 2019 fire, the restored nave gleams brighter than in living memory; entry is free, and the bell towers reopened in September 2025 for the climb to the gargoyles.

venues.name: Sainte-Chapelle
venues.note: A jewel-box royal chapel where fifteen soaring windows of 13th-century stained glass wrap you in coloured light, go on a bright morning for the full effect.
credentials: finest medieval stained glass in the world

venues.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
venues.note: The white domed basilica crowns the highest point in Paris; the steps below give one of the great free panoramas, and the dome climb rewards with a 360° sweep.

venues.name: Panthéon
venues.note: A neoclassical temple where France buries its greats, Voltaire, Curie, Hugo, with Foucault's pendulum swinging under the dome and a colonnade viewpoint above.

venues.name: Les Invalides & Napoleon's Tomb
venues.note: Under the gilded dome lies Napoleon in six nested coffins; the complex also holds the Army Museum, strong on the family history-of-France angle.

venues.name: Palais Garnier (Opéra)
venues.note: The most opulent theatre in Europe, grand staircase, gilded foyer, and a Chagall-painted ceiling; tour it by day or take an advisor-booked box for a ballet.
credentials: inspiration for Phantom of the Opera

venues.name: The Louvre
venues.note: The world's largest art museum; ask us to arrange an early-access or after-hours private hour so you meet the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo without the crush.

venues.name: Musée d'Orsay
venues.note: A grand Beaux-Arts railway station turned temple of Impressionism, Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Degas, best from the giant golden clock window on the top floor.
credentials: Finest Impressionist collection in the world

venues.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
venues.note: Two oval rooms hold Monet's monumental Water Lilies, wrapping you in eight curved panels designed by the painter himself, a meditative, unhurried half-hour.

venues.name: Musée Rodin
venues.note: The sculptor's mansion and rose garden, where The Thinker and The Kiss sit among clipped hedges, one of the loveliest, calmest museums in the city, ideal with children.

venues.name: Musée Picasso
venues.note: A restored 17th-century mansion in the Marais holding the world's greatest Picasso collection, drawn from the artist's own estate.

venues.name: Centre Pompidou
venues.note: The inside-out building of coloured pipes houses Europe's biggest modern-art museum; note it is closing for a multi-year renovation, so confirm access with us before you plan.

venues.name: Bourse de Commerce, Pinault Collection
venues.note: François Pinault's contemporary art inside a domed former grain exchange reimagined by Tadao Ando, a concrete cylinder within a historic rotunda; the 2026 show 'Clair-obscur' runs into late August.

venues.name: Musée Marmottan Monet
venues.note: The world's largest Monet holding, including 'Impression, Sunrise', the painting that named the movement, in an intimate townhouse well off the tourist track.

venues.name: Musée du Quai Branly, Jacques Chirac
venues.note: Jean Nouvel's museum of the arts of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas, wrapped in a living green wall, a thoughtful, less-obvious stop near the Eiffel Tower.

venues.name: Petit Palais
venues.note: The city's fine-arts museum in a jewel of a 1900 building, free entry, a gilded interior, and a serene garden café most visitors walk right past.

venues.name: Grand Palais
venues.note: Reopened in 2024 after a sweeping restoration, its vast glass-and-iron nave is Paris's grandest exhibition hall, check what blockbuster show is on.

venues.name: Musée Nissim de Camondo
venues.note: A perfectly preserved aristocratic mansion of 18th-century French decorative arts, with a moving family history, a quiet gem beside Parc Monceau.
credentials: House museum of the Camondo family

venues.name: Musée Jacquemart-André
venues.note: A collector couple's opulent townhouse hung with Italian and French masters; take tea in the frescoed dining room under a Tiepolo ceiling.

venues.name: Le Marais
venues.note: The best-preserved old quarter, Renaissance mansions, the arcaded Place des Vosges, designer boutiques and falafel lanes; wander with no plan, it rewards it.

venues.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
venues.note: Literary Left Bank of Café de Flore and Les Deux Magots, antique galleries and the city's oldest church, the neighbourhood for a slow morning and good browsing.

venues.name: Montmartre
venues.note: The village on the hill, cobbled lanes, the last working vineyard in Paris, artists in Place du Tertre, and hidden squares away from the crowds if you climb early.

venues.name: Île Saint-Louis
venues.note: A serene 17th-century island in the Seine, one main street of mansions and small shops, stroll the quays with a Berthillon ice cream, a Paris rite.

venues.name: Canal Saint-Martin
venues.note: Iron footbridges, plane trees and locks lined with young Paris; walk the canal to Bassin de la Villette, or take a slow boat cruise through the underground vaults.

venues.name: Latin Quarter & Rue Mouffetard
venues.note: Student Paris around the Sorbonne, plus the sloping market street of Rue Mouffetard, one of the oldest in the city, lined with cheese, wine and produce stalls.

venues.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
venues.note: The most beloved park in Paris, sail a toy boat on the fountain, watch a puppet show, and sit in the green chairs among statues and orchards; children adore it.

venues.name: Jardin des Tuileries
venues.note: The grand formal garden linking the Louvre to Place de la Concorde; ponds, statues and, in summer, a fairground with a big wheel over the treetops.

venues.name: Palais-Royal Gardens
venues.note: A hidden arcaded courtyard behind the Louvre, Buren's striped columns, lime-tree walks and old-world boutiques; one of the quietest lovely corners in the centre.

venues.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
venues.note: The most dramatic park in Paris, cliffs, a lake, a temple on a crag and a suspension bridge; a local, family-filled escape far from the tourist centre.

venues.name: Bois de Boulogne & Fondation Louis Vuitton
venues.note: Paris's great western woodland for boating and gardens, now anchored by Frank Gehry's glass-sail Fondation Louis Vuitton, a landmark of art and architecture in itself.

venues.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
venues.note: A hilly garden-necropolis of cobbled avenues and grand tombs, Chopin, Wilde, Piaf, Jim Morrison; strangely peaceful and beautiful, especially in autumn.

venues.name: Galeries Lafayette Rooftop
venues.note: Under the great stained-glass dome of the flagship store, then up to the free rooftop terrace for one of the best open-air views of the Opéra and Eiffel Tower.

venues.name: Montparnasse Tower Observation Deck
venues.note: The one skyline view that includes the Eiffel Tower, the 56th-floor deck and open rooftop give the finest sunset panorama in the city, minus the queues of the tower itself.
credentials: Tallest observation deck in central Paris

venues.name: The Covered Passages
venues.note: Glass-roofed 19th-century arcades, Galerie Vivienne, Passage des Panoramas, Passage Jouffroy, full of mosaic floors, old bookshops and tearooms; a rainy-day treasure hunt.

venues.name: Marché d'Aligre
venues.note: One of the liveliest, most authentic markets, a covered hall of fine cheese and produce plus an open-air flea market; go with us for a chef-led tasting stroll.

venues.name: Rue Cler Market Street
venues.note: A pretty pedestrian market street of cheesemongers, bakeries and florists near the Eiffel Tower, the classic spot to assemble a picnic for the Champ de Mars.

venues.name: Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen
venues.note: The world's largest antiques market, a sprawling maze of dealer stands in vintage furniture, art and curiosities; an advisor guide makes the labyrinth worthwhile.
credentials: World's largest antiques and flea market

venues.name: Bouquinistes of the Seine
venues.note: The green riverside book boxes are a UNESCO-listed Paris institution, browse antique prints, posters and old books along the quays between the bridges.

venues.name: Seine Dinner Cruise
venues.note: Glide past the floodlit monuments over a fine dinner; we book the private or premium boats, and can arrange a fully vegetarian or Jain-aware menu on board.

venues.name: Avenue Montaigne
venues.note: The couture spine of Paris, Dior, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Valentino, flagship after flagship; we can arrange private in-store appointments and after-hours access.

venues.name: Rue Saint-Honoré & Place Vendôme
venues.note: From Colette concept-store cool to the high-jewellery houses of Place Vendôme, Cartier, Van Cleef, Boucheron, set around the Ritz; the address for jewels and watches.

venues.name: Le Bon Marché
venues.note: The world's first department store and still the most refined, with La Grande Épicerie next door for one of the great food halls in Paris.

venues.name: Atelier des Lumières
venues.note: A former foundry turned immersive digital art hall where masterpieces sweep across the walls and floor to music, a hit with children and the whole family.

venues.name: Promenade Plantée (Coulée Verte)
venues.note: The elevated garden walkway on a disused railway viaduct, the inspiration for New York's High Line, running above the arch-shops of the Viaduc des Arts.

venues.name: Philharmonie de Paris
venues.note: Jean Nouvel's silver concert hall with world-class acoustics; we secure seats for an evening of the Orchestre de Paris or a visiting name.

venues.name: A Jazz Cave in Saint-Germain
venues.note: Descend into a vaulted stone cellar like Caveau de la Huchette or Le Duc des Lombards for late live jazz, an intimate, only-in-Paris night out.

venues.name: Palace of Versailles
venues.note: The supreme royal palace, Hall of Mirrors, the State Apartments, and vast formal gardens with the musical fountain shows; ask us for a private guide and skip-the-line timing.

venues.name: Château de Chantilly
venues.note: A fairytale château in a moat, holding the finest old-master collection outside the Louvre, plus the Great Stables and a Le Nôtre park, quieter than Versailles.

venues.name: Château de Fontainebleau
venues.note: A royal residence for eight centuries, from Francis I to Napoleon, sumptuous, uncrowded, and set in a vast forest ideal for a family walk or ride.

venues.name: Bar Hemingway, The Ritz Paris
venues.note: Twenty-five seats, a legend at the shaker, and the most storied cocktail room in Paris.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery

venues.name: Bar Nouveau
venues.note: The highest-ranked bar in Paris right now, Art Nouveau brought to life, drink by drink.

venues.name: The Cambridge Public House
venues.note: A British pub reimagined by serious bartenders, warm, unpretentious, world-class.

venues.name: Danico
venues.note: Velvet and gold in a covered arcade, precise cocktails behind Daniele Dalla Pola's counter.

venues.name: Little Red Door
venues.note: For a decade one of the world's most decorated bars, conceptual menus, faultless execution.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, No. 6 (2023); 51–100 list (No. 59, 2024)

venues.name: Candelaria
venues.note: The bar that began the Paris speakeasy era, a taqueria out front, a hidden room behind.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, repeat listee (peak No. 9, 2013); Top 500 Bars 2025

venues.name: Le Syndicat
venues.note: French spirits only, Cognac, Calvados, Armagnac, behind a deliberately shabby door.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, recent listee (No. 68, 2023)

venues.name: Cravan
venues.note: Franck Audoux's study of pre-1930s French cocktails, in a listed Art Nouveau corner house.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery; Difford's Guide top-50 bar

venues.name: Combat
venues.note: A female-led room, light and green, from alumni of the Experimental Cocktail Club.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery

venues.name: Le Tout-Paris, Cheval Blanc Paris
venues.area: 1st arr. / La Samaritaine, by the Seine
venues.note: The seventh-floor terrace of an LVMH palace, from Notre-Dame to the Eiffel Tower.
credentials: Inside Cheval Blanc Paris (French Palace distinction)

venues.name: Les Ombres
venues.note: A glass rooftop under Jean Nouvel's roof, with the Eiffel Tower almost close enough to touch.
